body.statement:
Fix \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), and \(0<M_1<\sqrt{M_2}\), and put \(\beta:=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\).  There are constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{unif}}\le C_{\mathrm{unif}}<\infty\) and \(T_0<\infty\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\), such that, simultaneously for every \(C\ge1\) and \(T\ge T_0\),
\[
 c_{\mathrm{unif}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}
 \le R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
 \le C_{\mathrm{unif}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}.
\]
The upper bound is attained by the observable tagged estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T(C)}\).  The lower bound holds against every tagged measurable decision family and already on the bounded, binary-action scaled signed-depth subclass.  Hence the exact elbow is \(q_C\asymp T^{-1/2}\), and no logarithmic factor occurs.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(r:=\log(1/\alpha)=1/t_0\), \(D_0:=2r+\log L\), and \(x:=Tq_C^2\).  Since \(L=e^\zeta\),
\[
 \beta=\frac{2r}{D_0}=\frac2{2+t_0\zeta},
 \qquad
 1-\beta=\frac{\log L}{D_0}. \tag{22}
\]

For the upper bound, apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}moment\text{-}phiw\text{-}radius\text{-}bound}\).  Because \(L>1\), its geometric sum is bounded by \(L^{k+1}/(L-1)\).  If \(k\le T/2\), there is a constant \(A<\infty\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\), such that
\[
 \sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)}
 E_M[(\widehat\theta_k-\theta(K,e))^2]
 \le A\{q_C^2\alpha^{2k}+T^{-1}L^k+T^{-1}\}. \tag{23}
\]
Choose \(T_0\) so large that \(\log T/D_0\le T/2\) for every \(T\ge T_0\).  Since \(0\le q_C<1\), the cap in \(\kappa_T(C)\) is then inactive whenever \(x>1\).

If \(x\le1\), \(\kappa_T(C)=0\), and (23) is at most a constant multiple of \(T^{-1}\), because \(q_C^2\le T^{-1}\).  If \(x>1\), set \(k=\lfloor\log x/D_0\rfloor\).  Then
\[
 \alpha^{2k}\le\alpha^{-2}x^{-\beta},
 \qquad
 L^k\le x^{1-\beta}. \tag{24}
\]
Consequently both nonparametric terms in (23) have the same value up to a fixed factor:
\[
 q_C^2x^{-\beta}=T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)},
 \qquad
 T^{-1}x^{1-\beta}=T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}. \tag{25}
\]
Equations (23)--(25) prove the asserted uniform upper bound and exhibit the single observable estimator.  No alphabet cardinality enters any constant.

We turn to the converse.  The parametric component is \(\mathrm{lem{:}parametric\text{-}moment\text{-}floor}\).  For the hidden-state component, let \(B_0\) be the \(C\)-independent constant in \(\mathrm{lem{:}scaled\text{-}observed\text{-}path\text{-}kl}\).  Choose a finite \(x_0\ge1\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta\), so that
\[
 Q_x:=\left\lceil D_0^{-1}\log(8B_0x)\right\rceil\ge1
\]
whenever \(x\ge x_0\).  The epsilon comparison in \(\mathrm{lem{:}scaled\text{-}signed\text{-}depth\text{-}radius}\) and the explicit KL modulus give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q_x,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\|\mathbb P_{Q_x,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})
 \le B_0T\varepsilon_C^2e^{-D_0Q_x}
 \le B_0xe^{-D_0Q_x}\le\frac18. \tag{26}
\]
The same membership lemma gives target values \(\pm a_Q\), where \(a_Q=c_0\varepsilon_Cw_Q\), and
\[
 w_Q=\frac{(1-\alpha)\alpha^Q}{1-\alpha^{Q+1}}
 \ge(1-\alpha)\alpha^Q. \tag{27}
\]
The testing inequality \(\mathrm{lem{:}two\text{-}point\text{-}testing\text{-}overlap}\) applies directly to this common-design pair.  The ceiling defining \(Q_x\) gives
\[
 \alpha^{2Q_x}\ge\alpha^2(8B_0x)^{-\beta}. \tag{28}
\]
Using (26)--(28) and \(\varepsilon_C\ge q_C/2\), we obtain a constant \(c_{\mathrm{hid}}>0\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\), such that for \(x\ge x_0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
 &\ge \frac14e^{-1/8}c_0^2\varepsilon_C^2(1-\alpha)^2\alpha^{2Q_x}\\
 &\ge c_{\mathrm{hid}}q_C^2x^{-\beta}
 =c_{\mathrm{hid}}T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{29}
\]
The scaled signed-depth alternatives are bounded and binary-action members of the broader arbitrary-finite-action conditional-moment class.  Therefore their two-point lower bound transfers to the supremum over that class; no restriction of the upper theorem has been introduced.

If \(x<x_0\), the hidden term satisfies
\[
 T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}=T^{-1}x^{1-\beta}
 \le x_0^{1-\beta}T^{-1},
\]
and is absorbed by the parametric lower bound.  If \(x\ge x_0\), the maximum of the parametric and hidden lower bounds is at least half their sum.  This proves the uniform lower inequality.  At \(C=1\), \(q_C=0\), so the law reduces to \(R_T\asymp T^{-1}\).  For each fixed \(C>1\), \(q_C\) is a positive constant and \(\beta<1\), so it reduces to \(R_T\asymp T^{-\beta}\).  These are respectively the equality and fixed-overlap corollaries of the same uniform theorem.  Finally, the ratio of the hidden term to \(T^{-1}\) is \(x^{1-\beta}\), so the unique elbow is \(Tq_C^2\asymp1\), equivalently \(q_C\asymp T^{-1/2}\).  The geometric covariance sum and the integer floor bounds introduce only constants, proving the absence of a logarithmic factor.
body.justification: This is the headline exact risk law with a radius-adaptive observable estimator and a matching converse uniform over the full overlap range.
body.gap: HuWager2023 has no latent-overlap-radius phase diagram and leaves the overlapping hidden-state converse open.
body.consumer: It quantifies exactly when a latent physiological occupancy assurance changes PHIW history and precision.
